Chapter 11: Temporality—Living Toward the Future
Time isn’t just a series of moments ticking by on a clock. It’s really the framework of human existence—the way our lives unfold from the past into the future.
We’re always moving forward, aren’t we? Constantly imagining what’s next, projecting ourselves into the days and years ahead.
Picture yourself at a crossroads, a little unsure about which way to go. You remember the choices you’ve made, you think about what could happen if you pick one path or another, and you feel the pressure of this exact moment. That feeling—of being stretched between what’s behind you and what might be—is what gives your life its shape.
Most of the time, we don’t even notice this structure. We’re swept up in daily events, reacting, making plans, chasing after goals. But when we stop and really reflect, it becomes obvious: we’re always living in that space between where we’ve been and where we’re going.
The past isn’t just a collection of old memories. It’s what shapes who we are—the habits we carry, the stories we tell ourselves, the lessons we’ve learned. And the future? That’s always wide open, full of possibility. Every single moment gives us a chance to choose, to make a change, to become something new.
Now, this openness can be exhilarating—it’s what gives us hope. But let’s be honest, it’s also kind of terrifying, isn’t it? Nothing is set in stone. Everything can change. With that freedom to choose comes the weight of responsibility. Most of us try to dodge that weight, sticking to familiar routines, searching for anything that feels certain. But every time we look ahead and really face the future, we rediscover what it means to live authentically.
So, temporality isn’t just some abstract philosophical idea. It’s the real, lived experience of being human. Life is always in motion, always unfinished, always becoming. If you want to live fully, you’ve got to embrace that movement—accepting both the risks and the endless possibilities waiting in the future.
